notes: Will contest over testamentary capacity; testator's having operated a rooming house is mentioned only as biographical background (part of her being a 'hard-working, industrious woman'), with no adjudication of any lodging/letting issue.

holding_summary: The Court of Civil Appeals held that a homeowner's temporary rental of a second house on his homestead lot to a tenant did not, as a matter of law, defeat the homestead exemption as to that house. An owner is entitled to a reasonable time after purchase to occupy the whole of a homestead lot, and temporary renting of part of it pending consolidation of the buildings does not conclusively show abandonment. Whether the renting was temporary (and thus consistent with continued homestead use) or evidenced a permanent commercial diversion was a fact question for the jury.

notes: Concerns a full separate house rented to a tenant on part of a homestead lot, not room-letting to lodgers/boarders in an owner-occupied dwelling; included because the court treats temporary letting of part of one's property as an ordinary, non-disqualifying incident of ownership rather than abandonment or commercial diversion. Duration is approximate (at least ~3 months at time of levy; tenant's occupancy predated the purchase).

Tort case on scope-of-employment liability for an employee's assault; 'rooming house' appears only once, identifying where the injured brakeman intended to go after work, with no bearing on lodging law.

Mineral deed construction dispute over royalty/bonus/rental fractions from an oil and gas lease; 'lease' here refers exclusively to a mineral lease, unrelated to dwelling occupancy.

Validity-of-spot-zoning case concerning rezoning a small tract to local retail; a 'tourist court' is mentioned only in passing as one existing use on nearby already-rezoned lots, with no adjudication of any lodging-related right or regulation.
Master-servant premises-liability case (employee slip-and-fall on spilled oil in a warehouse); the citation to Houston National Bank v. Adair concerns a stairway, not lodging.

Contempt proceeding over an alleged sham lease/sale between brothers used to evade a non-compete covenant in the wholesale gasoline business; the string citation to Owen v. Willis regarding restrictive covenants is incidental and unrelated to dwelling letting.
Contract dispute over a cigarette-supply agreement tied to the sale of corporate stock; 'incident to the ownership thereof' refers to stock ownership, not any dwelling or room-letting arrangement.
Mandamus action over the State's mineral royalty reservation and oil/gas leasing rights under public land sales acts; entirely a mineral-lease/royalty dispute, unrelated to dwelling occupancy.

Fraud/limitations dispute arising from the sale of a tourist court whose highway frontage title was misrepresented; the tourist court is only an incidental identifier of the property sold, and the holding concerns discovery of fraud and limitations, not any lodging-related right or regulation.
Mineral-deed/pooling case concerning whether production elsewhere in a unit extends a term mineral interest; no lodging or dwelling-letting issue.

Mineral-deed construction dispute between two conflicting deeds over the fraction of minerals conveyed; unrelated to dwelling letting.

Suit to enforce a 'residence purposes only' restrictive covenant against a tract where churches had been built nearby; concerns waiver/changed-conditions doctrine as to church use, with no boarding-house or paying-lodger issue present.
Challenge to a zoning ordinance banning front-yard fences on police-power grounds (traffic safety, firefighting access, crime prevention); no lodging or boarding-house regulation involved.

The underlying dispute concerns a city's attempt to enjoin use of land as a 'trailer coach park' / 'mobile home residence area' under a zoning ordinance, but the only issue actually decided here is res judicata (whether a prior judgment bars the new suit); the case is reversed and remanded for trial on the merits without any holding on the legality or characterization of the trailer-park use. Also, a trailer/mobile-home park (renting parking spaces) is a distinct use-type from letting rooms or dwellings to lodgers/boarders, so even a merits holding here would only be loosely analogous.

Suit for damages from diversion of dedicated parkland to highway construction; 'tourist court units' are mentioned only as improvements the plaintiff purchased on the abutting property, with no adjudication of any lodging-related right or regulation.
